channel.title: Reddy Pulse — Akhil Reddy Danda
channel.description: Daily tech takes and AI startup blueprints by Akhil Reddy Danda.

item.title: Agentic Coding: What Actually Works and What’s Just Hype in 2026
item.description: Developers are moving beyond the 'copilot' gimmick, and the daily grind with Claude Code and eval-driven loops is reshaping how we ship software. This is what actually matters for engineers doing the work.

item.title: Inference Costs and the Silicon Wars: Why Every Engineer Should Care
item.description: AI inference costs are now as important as model size, and the silicon arms race is shifting how we think about deployment. If you ship AI, these realities should shape every design decision.

item.title: What Microsoft Should Steal Next: Deep Integration Evals and Real Agent Tooling
item.description: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google are racing ahead with eval stacks and agent tool APIs. Microsoft needs to rethink how Copilot, Azure AI, and GitHub handle agent evaluation and tool orchestration—here’s why.

item.title: Agentic Coding in 2026: Loops, Specs, and the Real Workflows Shaping AI Dev
item.description: Agentic coding isn't hype—it's everyday practice now. Developers drive AI with tightly-looped evaluation, live MCP tool servers, and spec-driven prompts, using Claude and open alternatives for real code shipping.

item.title: Datacenter Crunch: GPUs, Supply, and the Energy Wall Facing AI
item.description: GPU supply is tight, inference costs are rising, and the energy ceiling is real. Why compute constraints are now shaping not just deployment but fundamental AI product design.

item.title: Microsoft Needs OpenAI’s Multi-Agent EvalStack: Here’s Why
item.description: OpenAI's EvalStack and orchestrated multi-agent workflows are outperforming single Copilot flows. Microsoft must embrace this shift for Azure and GitHub to compete in real-world enterprise AI.

item.title: DANDA #072 — PrepPro AI: Autonomous Agents to End School Meal Planning Chaos and Cost Waste
item.description: School districts waste millions on inefficient meal planning and supply mismanagement—PrepPro AI deploys autonomous agents to optimize menus, purchasing, and compliance in real time for every cafeteria.

item.title: Agentic Coding with Claude: How Eval-Driven Loops are Reshaping Developer Work
item.description: AI agents are no longer just copilots—they’re hands-on coders. The rise of Claude Code, MCP tool servers, and eval-driven loops is changing how we ship software, not someday, but right now.

item.title: GPUs, Inference Costs, and Why Energy is the Next Bottleneck for AI Engineers
item.description: AI’s appetite for compute keeps growing, but we’re hitting hard limits on GPU supply, energy, and datacenter expansion. What do these constraints mean for devs shipping real AI apps?

item.title: What Microsoft Should Steal Next From the Frontier Labs (And Why We Need It)
item.description: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google are moving fast on model control, evals, and agentic architectures. Here’s what Microsoft (and Azure) should copy or adapt—now.

item.title: DANDA #071 — ArtGuard AI: End Art Gallery Inventory Chaos and Theft Risk with Autonomous Agentic Automation
item.description: ArtGuard AI tackles the persistent nightmare of art gallery inventory mismanagement, theft risk, and insurance disputes. Every year, galleries lose millions to inventory mistakes, misplaced artworks, and unresolved claims. This agent automates inventory tracking, provenance validation, and theft prevention—bringing gold-standard oversight to every collection with zero paperwork.

item.title: Microsoft Graph Copilot Mesh: Unified Data Context for Enterprise AI
item.description: Microsoft just announced Graph Copilot Mesh, a major expansion of Microsoft Graph that finally unifies data access and context for all AI copilots across the Microsoft stack. This is a big deal for engineers building real-world AI apps at scale.

item.title: AMD CDNA4 Ships: 8nm AI GPUs Built for Multi-LLM Orchestration
item.description: AMD just launched the first CDNA4 GPUs on their new 8nm process with specialized tensor clusters for orchestrating multiple LLM inference jobs. This release finally gives hyperscalers a real alternative to NVIDIA for large-scale AI serving.

item.title: Claude Sonnet 128K: Real-World, Reliable Long-Context Reasoning Arrives
item.description: Anthropic’s new Claude Sonnet 128K is the first mainstream LLM to deliver reliable, not just nominal, long-context reasoning—making 100K+ tokens actually useful for engineering and research workflows.

item.title: DANDA #070 — ShiftWise: AI Agents to End Retail Shift-Swap Chaos and Absenteeism
item.description: Millions of retail workers still swap or miss shifts via clunky group texts, paper calendars, or unreliable apps—leading to understaffed stores, lost sales, and high turnover. ShiftWise delivers agentic automation that fills gaps, negotiates swaps, and keeps stores running smoothly with zero drama.

item.title: SQL Server 2027 Preview Ships Native Vector Search: Why RDBMS Matters for AI Apps
item.description: Microsoft just dropped the SQL Server 2027 preview, and the big headline is vector search as a first-class citizen. This isn’t just a nod to AI trendiness—RDBMS-native vectors fundamentally change how engineers can build and reason about AI-powered apps.

item.title: Samsung’s 3nm Gate-All-Around Hits Mass Production: Why FETs Just Got Interesting Again
item.description: Samsung has started mass-producing chips on their 3nm Gate-All-Around (GAA) process. This is a big deal for AI hardware and power efficiency obsessed engineers.

item.title: Meta’s Falcon-400B Drops: Open-Weights, Long Context, and Real Reasoning Progress
item.description: Meta just released Falcon-400B, a 400-billion parameter LLM with open weights. But parameter count isn’t the headline—this model finally pushes open LLMs close to GPT-4 in reasoning, with a 256K context window.

item.title: DANDA #069 — ClaimWise Vet: Autonomous Agents to End Veterans' Benefits Backlog
item.description: Over 1.2 million US veterans are stuck in a maze of delayed or denied benefits, losing years to unprocessed claims. ClaimWise Vet is the first agentic automation platform that ingests, organizes, and advocates for veterans’ disability, pension, and healthcare claims—cutting through paperwork, errors, and government bottlenecks.

item.title: Microsoft Dataverse Gets Embedded Databricks, Smashing Data Silos for App Devs
item.description: Microsoft just rolled out direct Databricks workspace integration inside Dataverse. For engineers, this means no more brittle ETL pipelines between low-code apps and serious analytics workloads.

item.title: Apple Cherry M1: On-Package Photonics Comes to Consumer Laptops
item.description: Apple's new Cherry M1 chip just dropped with integrated silicon photonics. This might finally make optical interconnects a thing outside the datacenter.

item.title: Mistral’s Mixtralit 6x24B: Sparse Mixture Models Go Open-Source, Outperforming Dense Giants
item.description: Mistral just open-sourced Mixtralit 6x24B, a massive sparse Mixture-of-Experts LLM that matches (and sometimes beats) closed dense models twice its size. This is a pivotal moment for open AI research.

item.title: DANDA #068 — ClaimWise AI: End Disability Benefits Backlog with Autonomous Filing and Tracking
item.description: Millions of Americans with disabilities are trapped by a broken, manual benefits system. ClaimWise AI is a fully autonomous agent that files, tracks, and corrects disability claims end-to-end—cutting wait times, reducing denials, and unlocking billions in life-saving support.

item.title: Microsoft Copilot Studio Launches on macOS: Why It’s Actually a Big Deal
item.description: Microsoft’s Copilot Studio—a no-code/low-code AI agent builder—just landed natively on macOS with persistent local sandboxing and cross-platform plugin support. This isn’t just a port; it’s a statement about AI development workflows.

item.title: ARM Unveils v11 Architecture: First-Class Inference Accelerators and Dataflow Cores
item.description: ARM just dropped the technical preview for v11—a sweeping new architecture with native on-die inference accelerators and the first real dataflow cores in a mainstream CPU.

item.title: OpenAI’s GPT-5 Hybrid Memory: Long-Context Meets Fast-Context Without the Latency Tax
item.description: OpenAI researchers just published details about GPT-5’s hybrid memory architecture—a two-tiered attention system that promises fast token throughput and massive context retention, simultaneously.

item.title: DANDA #067 — ClaimSafe AI: End Lost & Damaged Package Claim Chaos for Online Shoppers
item.description: Americans lost or received damage to over 2 billion shipped packages last year, but filing claims with carriers remains an opaque, time-wasting, and frustrating labyrinth for both consumers and small retailers. ClaimSafe AI is an agentic automation platform that instantly manages lost or damaged package claims start-to-finish, slashing resolution time from weeks to hours, recovering billions in refunds, and restoring trust in e-commerce.

item.title: Microsoft OrbitGraph: Native Graph Compute in Azure Data Lake
item.description: Microsoft just announced OrbitGraph, a graph-native compute engine for Azure Data Lake, making connected data analysis a first-class citizen across the cloud. This is a big deal for anyone building systems that rely on relationships, not just rows.

item.title: NVIDIA Blackwell Refresh: HBM4 Memory Breaks the 4TB/s Barrier
item.description: NVIDIA's Blackwell Refresh GPUs with HBM4 are the first accelerators to smash through 4TB/s memory bandwidth, redefining what engineers can do with AI and simulation workloads. The hardware bar for 'memory-bound' just got obliterated.

item.title: Google Sparrow-2: On-the-Fly Contextual Planning in Large Language Models
item.description: The new Google Sparrow-2 LLM can generate, chain, and revise multi-step plans inside a single context window, making it a leap forward for agents and real-world workflow automation. This is the closest thing yet to a generalist 'reasoning engine.'

item.title: DANDA #066 — LoanPrep AI: End Small Business SBA Loan Rejection Due to Documentation Chaos
item.description: Turning rejected SBA loan applications into approvals by automating documentation, eligibility checks, and agentic compliance for America’s 5M+ small businesses.

item.title: Edge Workspaces FileKernel: The New Filesystem for the Web Era
item.description: Microsoft’s Edge team just announced FileKernel, a radical browser-native filesystem that blurs the line between web apps and the local OS. This changes how engineers should think about file APIs and user data handling.

item.title: Intel Crystal4: Microarchitectural Reboot Targets AI Workloads
item.description: Intel’s Crystal4 CPUs mark their boldest core redesign in a decade, throwing out legacy baggage for a reconfigurable, AI-centric execution pipeline. This is the x86 pivot engineers have been waiting for.

item.title: Anthropic’s Context Vault: 200M Token Windows Open Up New App Frontiers
item.description: Anthropic’s new Context Vault tech smashes the context window bottleneck, letting Claude models handle up to 200 million tokens. This isn’t just a party trick — it changes how engineers can build RAG, code, and analytics apps.

item.title: DANDA #065 — HealthClaimAI: AI Agents to End FSA/HSA Reimbursement Rejection Hell
item.description: Americans forfeit over $1.7 billion annually in unused Flexible Spending Account (FSA) and Health Savings Account (HSA) funds, frequently due to claim submission mistakes, missing receipts, or misunderstood eligibility rules. HealthClaimAI is an autonomous AI agent that intercepts, validates, and files health-related purchases in real-time—eliminating rejected claims, lost savings, and paperwork frustration for 70+ million FSA/HSA holders.

item.title: Windows HyperLight UI: Real-Time Adaptive Interfaces Arrive
item.description: Microsoft quietly rolled out the HyperLight UI system in the latest Windows Insider build, radically changing how the OS adapts to hardware and user context in real time. This matters for engineers because it unlocks new kinds of desktop and hybrid apps.

item.title: Samsung 1.6A: Gate-All-Around Hits Production, Shrinking AI Edge Chips Again
item.description: Samsung's new 1.6A process is now in mass production, marking the first commercial Gate-All-Around (GAA) node below 2nm. This will reshape edge AI hardware design for the next five years.

item.title: Meta’s Falcon-LLaMA Mixture: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts at Scale
item.description: Meta AI just open-sourced Falcon-LLaMA, its sparse MoE model that mixes LLaMA’s reasoning with Falcon’s data efficiency. This is a new playbook for fast, cheap, and surprisingly robust LLMs.

item.title: DANDA #064 — UtilityHelp: AI Agents to End Household Utility Bill Shock and Missed Assistance
item.description: Every year, tens of millions of American households face utility shutoffs or crippling energy debt due to skyrocketing bills and missed access to assistance programs. UtilityHelp is an AI-powered agent that proactively audits utility bills, predicts bill shock, automatically applies for aid, and negotiates with providers—no paperwork, jargon, or missed deadlines.

item.title: Microsoft Foundation Models Launchpad: Custom LLMs as a Service Go Live
item.description: Microsoft quietly launched Foundation Models Launchpad, a managed platform for deploying, fine-tuning, and serving custom large language models on Azure. This is a massive step in democratizing private, scalable LLMs for every engineering team—not just AI giants.
